title: Private cookie nonces can repeat in processes that fork
description: This vulnerability affects Rust applications that use the cookie crate to add private (encrypted) cookies on a thread that forks into multiple processes without an exec. The nonce used for AES-256-GCM encryption of private cookies can be reused in the parent and child processes, breaking the security guarantees of AES-GCM. This nonce reuse allows an attacker to recover plaintext relationships and forge private cookies. The issue only affects Unix-like systems with fork without exec, and only the first 21 private cookies added after the fork on the same thread share nonces. Applications that do not fork, use signed cookies, or use versions 0.12.0 and later of the cookie crate are not affected. Rocket and axum frameworks are generally not affected unless axum is used with a specific forking and runtime configuration. The vulnerability is fixed in cookie crate version 0.18.3.
